This is repair and overhaul work. Parts and machines come in to you and go back out to specification, with the technical drawing as your reference. You disassemble them, assess what's worn or damaged, replace what needs replacing, and rebuild the whole as specified by the drawing. Overhaul work calls for a different kind of craftsmanship than building something new. You don't know in advance what you'll find, so your judgement determines what's needed. Anyone already doing this work in high-tech metalworking knows the difference. Repairing parts and machines according to technical drawings; Disassembling and assessing incoming parts; Carrying out overhaul work and replacing worn or damaged parts; Rebuilding and checking that everything is back to specification; Recording your findings and the work carried out.
